sentences.text: Abdarainurus is a genus of titanosaur dinosaur known from eight front tail vertebrae, one middle tail vertebra, and several chevrons.
These fossils represent a fragmentary skeleton of tail vertebrae and haemal arches, possessing 16 unique and diagnostic anatomical features.
The holotype specimen PIN 5669/1 was discovered in 1970 in Abdrant Nuru during a Joint Soviet–Mongolian Paleontological expedition and excavated by V. P. Tverdokhlebov.
The species Abdarainurus barsboldi was formally named in February 2020 and described in honor of the Mongolian paleontologist Rinchengin Barsbold.
Averianov and Lopatin suggested that Abdarainurus was most likely a basal titanosaur based on having the fewest unique features in their analysis.
The genus name Abdarainurus means "Abdrant Nuru tail," derived from the Russian pronunciation of the locality Abdrant Nuru and the Greek word for tail.
Abdarainurus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 85 million years ago in the Santonian stage, in what is now Asia.
The time range for Abdarainurus is estimated from 85.7 to 72.2 million years ago, spanning the Santonian to Campanian stages.
Abdarainurus coexisted with the ankylosaur Pinacosaurus sp., as well as indeterminate turtles and dinosaurs.
